look_here_first: Look for the flower architecture: five red petals remain tightly furled rather than spreading flat, while the staminal column and style project conspicuously beyond them. Then confirm the stellate-hairy, cordate to shallowly 3-lobed leaves.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: stellate hairs on stems and leaf veins

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: bright red hibiscus-like flowers whose petals remain tightly furled

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: inferior? no — superior multi-carpellate ovary typical of Malvaceae; avoid confusing the projecting staminal column with the style alone

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: fleshy red segmented fruit at maturity

key_traits.label: Flower
key_traits.text: Five petals stay wrapped/furled; numerous stamens are united into a conspicuous staminal column surrounding the style.

key_traits.label: Leaf morphology
key_traits.text: Broadly ovate to cordate, often shallowly 3-lobed, coarsely serrate-crenate, palmately veined and stellate-hairy.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Fleshy red schizocarp-like fruit composed of multiple mericarps.
